items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: him and I are good buddies. I go by and chew the rag with him, sit there and talk about old times.

ctx.x: -- I don't know -- I said, I think you ought to well, I said (unintelligible) make some records. He said no. So when he made that one, I was really surprised because he --

His eye hadn't bothered him that much then. But just since '72 he got worse. And so Doc tried to get him -- him and I are good buddies. I go by and chew the rag with him, sit there and talk about old times. And I coat him (unintelligible), come on, I'm going to come by. We go for a little walk. But I think he's conscious of the fact that his eye, you know, I guess he want to feel like that he's a burden on somebody. But he shouldn't. Look at Art Tatum. Look at them fellows.
Yes. But, of course, that's true, but then he was more or less -- he had that more or less from the time he was a child, didn't he, Tatum?
